newsitem.title: INDIA: Trinidad woos India business headed for S. America.
newsitem.headline: Trinidad woos India business headed for S. America.

text.p: Trinidad and Tobago Prime Minister Basdeo Panday said on Friday his country was a good platform for Indian businessmen to launch into South American markets.
Panday began a two-week visit to India on Friday with a ceremonial reception at the colonial-era Presidential Palace
He will be the chief guest at India's Republic Day celebrations on January 26.
"I have brought down with me a team of businessmen from the private sector," Panday told reporters after inspecting a guard of honour.

"They are going to have several meetings with their business counterparts and the object is two things -- to increase trade with Trinidad and Tobago and to see whether we can encourage investments from India to come to Trinidad.

"As you know Trinidad is...very close to South America. We understand Indian businessmen are interested in launching off into South America, and Trinidad will provide tremendous investment opportunities if they do so."
The two countries will sign an agreement on Friday to boost bilateral trade.
Indian Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah said earlier this week the trade pact would give exporters and investors in each country better access to the other's markets.
Panday is accompanied by Trinidad's ministers of Foreign Affairs, Ralph Maraj, and Trade and Industry, Mervyn Assam.
The 64-year-old lawyer and trade unionist, Trinidad and Tobago's first ethnic Indian prime minister, heads a coalition government.
Panday is the grandson of indentured labourers brought to work on British-owned sugar plantations in Trinidad in 1908.
"They have found my grandmother's village in India. So I intend to visit there," he said.
